prompt: Vertical photograph, cinematic, natural light. A young English woman in her mid-twenties, fair skin, light brown hair in a loose ponytail, walking toward the camera at a relaxed pace along a sunlit London pavement — pale stone and brick terraced buildings softly out of focus behind her, a plane tree, a few blurred passers-by far back. She wears a plain white t-shirt, a light-blue denim jacket, straight cream trousers and white trainers, a plain tan leather tote on her left shoulder. In her right hand a plain white paper coffee cup with a plain white lid; in her left hand a plain black smartphone, screen dark, and a small bunch of keys on a plain steel ring hanging from two fingers. Her expression is easy and unhurried, eyes ahead. Late-afternoon sun from camera-left, long soft shadows, warm highlights; shallow depth of field. Full body framed head to trainers with air above her head and pavement below her feet; nothing overlaps her. No text, no lettering, no logos, no printed matter, no signage anywhere in the image; the phone screen is dark and blank.

Continuous single take, handheld cinematic camera walking backwards slightly ahead of her, keeping her full body in frame the whole time; no cuts. Seconds 0 to 4: she walks toward the camera at a relaxed pace, sipping from the paper coffee cup once, phone and keys in her other hand, the street behind her drifting past. Seconds 4 to 5: a young man on a skateboard rolls in fast from frame-right and clips her shoulder as he passes; she is knocked half a step sideways, her arms fly up, and the coffee cup, the phone and the keys leave her hands. Seconds 5 to 10: time slows to extreme cinematic slow motion — the cup tumbling with an arc of coffee spilling out of it, the phone turning end over end, the keys spinning and catching the sun, all hanging in the air around her at head height while her hair and jacket lift; her face turns toward the flying cup, mouth open in surprise; the skateboarder blurs out of frame. The camera holds steady and slowly pushes in during the slow motion. Everything stays in the same sunlit street; same clothes, same face, same light. No text, no lettering, no logos.

Bright, playful, modern instrumental for a short social video: upbeat plucked synth and light percussion at a walking tempo, a clean break at the 4-second mark into a dreamy, slowed, reverb-washed half-time feel with a soft rising pad, no vocals, no drums fills, about 20 seconds.
